title: Auditing HNSW Index Leakage: Recovering Embedding Geometry from Graph Topology

contributions.purpose: Show that HNSW index topology leaks geometric information beyond the explicit adjacency lists.
contributions.mechanism: First systematic study framing leaked layer-0 HNSW adjacency graph as an attack surface, reconstructing approximate embedding geometry and comparing recovered kNN against raw adjacency lists.
contributions.evaluation: On MSMARCO-10K (768-d) the method recovers kNN better than adjacency-only baseline; ER random graph sanity check yields near-chance recall (269x lower than HNSW), confirming exploited metric structure.
contributions.domain: Vector database / RAG security (approximate nearest neighbor index privacy)
contributions.source_quote: The first systematic study of geometric information leakage from HNSW index topology, demonstrating that index files reveal more than raw adjacency lists.

contributions.purpose: Recover faithful metric distances from small-world graphs despite hub-induced shortcut distortion.
contributions.mechanism: Degree-penalized geodesic embedding: weight each edge by 1 + alpha * (log-degree average of endpoints) to penalize paths through high-degree hubs, compute landmark Dijkstra shortest paths, then apply landmark MDS with out-of-sample triangulation.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves Recall@10 of 0.4164 on MSMARCO-10K, a 28% relative improvement over adjacency-only (0.3248) and 52% over unweighted geodesic (0.2731); std <0.003 across seeds.
contributions.source_quote: A degree-penalized geodesic embedding algorithm that counteracts small-world shortcut distortion, achieving 28% improvement on high-dimensional text embeddings.

contributions.purpose: Characterize when topology leakage is most concerning across data dimensionality.
contributions.mechanism: Compare attack effectiveness on high-dimensional text embeddings (768-d MSMARCO) versus low-dimensional image descriptors (128-d SIFT10K).
contributions.evaluation: Attack improves over adjacency-only by 28% on MSMARCO-10K (768-d) but underperforms on SIFT10K (128-d, 0.2684 vs 0.3475), identifying high-dimensional RAG embeddings as the primary concern.
contributions.source_quote: Empirical characterization of dimension-dependent attack effectiveness, identifying high-dimensional embeddings as the primary concern for topology leakage.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work extends this line of research by demonstrating that HNSW index topology leaks geometric information beyond what is explicitly present in adjacency lists.

These methods assume access to true kNN relationships, whereas our setting provides only the HNSW approximation graph, which contains both true neighbors and small-world shortcuts that distort geodesic distances.
Our work complements these studies by demonstrating that even the index structure itself, independent of query access, can leak sensitive geometric information about the embedded documents.
The seminal work of Narayanan & Shmatikov (2009) demonstrated that social network topology alone can de-anonymize users by matching graph structure across networks.

notes: Mixed/negative on low-dimensional data: on SIFT10K (128-d) the adjacency-only baseline outperforms the proposed reconstruction (0.3475 vs 0.2684), and unweighted geodesic underperforms adjacency-only on both datasets.
